questions.question: A production line is controlled by CONWIP with a fixed number $n$ of cards, and every job on the shop floor holds a card. Under which rule may a new job enter the line?
options: As soon as the first station is idle, whatever the number of cards in use.
Only when a card is free, that is, after some job has left the line.
Only when the bottleneck station holds fewer than $n$ jobs in its queue.
At a fixed release rate chosen so that every station has load below one.

questions.question: In a CONWIP line with $n$ cards, new jobs wait in a backlog until a card is free. Which time interval of a job does the cycle time $\mathbb{E}[J(n)]=n/\mathrm{TH}_1(n)$ measure?
options: From joining the backlog until leaving the line, card wait included.
Only the total service time $T_0$, without any queueing at the stations.
From entering the line with a card until leaving the line again.
From leaving the line until its card is taken by the next new job.

questions.question: A planner models a production line as a CONWIP closed network and analyses it with mean value analysis (MVA). Which quantity does the planner choose, and what does the analysis deliver?
options: The card count $n$ is chosen; the throughput and cycle time follow.
The arrival rate is chosen; the card count follows from Little's law.
The throughput is chosen; the card count follows as $n=\mathrm{TH}_1T_0$, with $T_0$ the total service time per job.
The cycle time is chosen; the throughput is then $1/\mathbb{E}[J]$.

questions.question: A CONWIP line has $m$ single-server stations with exponential service times; station $i$ has visit ratio $V_i$ and mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$, the work per job $V_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]$ is not the same at every station, and $T_0=\sum_iV_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]$. How does the throughput $\mathrm{TH}_1(n)$ behave as the card count $n$ grows?
options: It grows in proportion to $n$, like $n/T_0$, without any upper limit.
It is largest when $n$ equals the number $m$ of stations and then falls.
It approaches $m/T_0$, the reciprocal of the mean work per station.
It rises towards $1/\max_iV_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]$ but never exceeds it.

questions.question: A CONWIP line can run with very few cards or with many cards. Compared with a large card count, what does a very small card count give?
options: Shorter cycle times and a higher throughput, because there is less congestion.
Longer cycle times, because each job first waits for a free card to enter.
Shorter cycle times, but servers are often idle, so the throughput is low.
The same throughput, since the bottleneck fixes the output for every $n$.

questions.question: A CONWIP line runs with $n=6$ cards, and mean value analysis gives the throughput $\mathrm{TH}_1(6)=0.4$ jobs per hour. What is the mean cycle time $\mathbb{E}[J(6)]$?
options: $2.4$ hours
$15$ hours
$2.5$ hours
$0.067$ hours

questions.question: A CONWIP line has three single-server stations, each visited once per job, with mean service times $3$, $2$ and $1$ hours. With a single card ($n=1$), what is the throughput $\mathrm{TH}_1(1)$?
options: $1/3$ job per hour
$11/6$ jobs per hour
$1/9$ job per hour
$1/6$ job per hour

questions.question: A CONWIP line with $n=6$ cards has four single-server stations, each visited once per job. Mean value analysis gives $\mathbb{E}[L_2(6)]=1.66$, $\mathbb{E}[L_3(6)]=0.78$ and $\mathbb{E}[L_4(6)]=0.29$ jobs. What is the mean number of jobs $\mathbb{E}[L_1(6)]$ at station 1?
options: $3.27$ jobs
$2.27$ jobs
$1.50$ jobs
$0.91$ jobs

questions.question: A deterministic line has five stations with service times $2$, $4$, $1$, $1$ and $2$ hours, each visited once per job. What is its critical WIP $W_0$, the number of jobs that keeps the bottleneck fully occupied without extra waiting?
options: $5$ jobs
$40$ jobs
$2.5$ jobs
$0.4$ jobs

questions.question: In a CONWIP line with $n=5$ cards, every job visits the single-server station 1 once, with mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=1.5$ hours there. Mean value analysis gives $\mathrm{TH}_1(5)=0.572$ jobs per hour. What fraction of time is station 1 busy?

A CONWIP line of $m\geq2$ stations has total work per cycle $T_0$ and a unique bottleneck station $b$ with the largest work per cycle $V_b\mathbb{E}[S_b]$. For a large card count $n$, roughly how much does one extra card add to the mean cycle time $\mathbb{E}[J(n)]$?
options: About $V_b\mathbb{E}[S_b]$, since the extra job mostly queues at the bottleneck.
About $T_0$, since the extra job needs one more full pass through the line.
Almost nothing, since the cycle time levels off just as the throughput does.
About $T_0/m$, the average work per station, shared over all the queues.

questions.question: A CONWIP line has $n=10$ cards, and a released card returns to the start at once. Customer orders sometimes run out, so no job is waiting when a card is released. What does this mean for modelling the line as a closed network with population 10?
options: The model still holds, since immediate card return is all that it requires.
The model still holds, provided the cycle time also counts the wait for cards.
The model still holds, as long as the throughput stays below the bottleneck rate.
The floor then sometimes holds fewer than 10 jobs, so the model overstates WIP.

questions.question: Mean value analysis (MVA) gives exact throughputs for a CONWIP line of single-server first-come-first-served stations with exponential service times. Which change to such a line makes the MVA results no longer exact?
options: Doubling the number of cards from 6 to 12 while keeping the stations.
Making service at one station deterministic, with the same mean as before.
Making one station's mean service time four times as long as the others.
Adding a rework loop, so that one station is visited $1.5$ times per job.

questions.question: A CONWIP loop has three single-server stations with mean service times $1$, $0.5$ and $2$ hours and visit ratios $V_1=1$, $V_2=3$ and $V_3=0.4$ per job. What is the upper limit $r_b$ on the throughput $\mathrm{TH}_1(n)$, whatever the card count?
options: $0.5$ job per hour
$1$ job per hour
$2/3$ job per hour
$0.303$ job per hour

questions.question: A CONWIP line with bottleneck rate $r_b=0.5$ jobs per hour must deliver at least $0.45$ jobs per hour. Mean value analysis gives $\mathrm{TH}_1(n)=0.412$, $0.438$, $0.456$ and $0.468$ jobs per hour for $n=4,5,6,7$ cards. What is the mean cycle time with the smallest card count that meets the target?
options: About $11.4$ hours
About $11.0$ hours
About $12.0$ hours
About $13.2$ hours

questions.question: A CONWIP line has total service time per cycle $T_0=7$ hours and bottleneck rate $r_b=0.25$ jobs per hour. A spreadsheet reports the mean cycle time $\mathbb{E}[J(10)]=34$ hours for $n=10$ cards. Is this value possible?
options: No: with 10 cards the cycle time is at least $n/r_b=40$ hours.
Yes: it exceeds $T_0=7$ hours, the lower bound on the cycle time.
Yes: it stays below $nT_0=70$ hours, a limit for the cycle time.
No: for this $n$ the cycle time must equal $n/r_b=40$ hours.

questions.question: A deterministic line holding its critical WIP $W_0=r_bT_0$ jobs keeps its bottleneck fully occupied. The service times are replaced by exponential ones with the same means, and the CONWIP card count stays near $W_0$. What happens to the throughput $\mathrm{TH}_1(n)$?
options: It stays at $r_b$, because MVA uses only the mean service times.
It falls below $r_b$, and fewer cards would restore it by cutting queues.
It falls well below $r_b$, as jobs sometimes bunch at faster stations.
It exceeds $r_b$, since short services sometimes speed up the bottleneck.

questions.question: In an open tandem line with arrival rate $\lambda$, the mean queues stay finite only if $\lambda<r_b$. A planner fears that a CONWIP line with many cards, modelled as a closed network with population $n$, can become unstable in the same way. Which statement about the shop floor is correct?
options: It becomes unstable once $n$ exceeds the critical WIP $r_bT_0$.
It stays stable for every $n$: it holds exactly $n$ jobs at all times.
It is stable only if $n/T_0<r_b$, the closed analogue of $\lambda<r_b$.
It becomes unstable once $n$ exceeds the number of stations.

questions.question: A CONWIP line has two single-server stations with exponential service times, means $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=2$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=1$ hours, each visited once per job. Using mean value analysis, what is the throughput $\mathrm{TH}_1(2)$ with two cards?
options: $1/2$ job per hour
$2/3$ job per hour
$1/3$ job per hour
$3/7$ job per hour

questions.question: A CONWIP line has total service time per cycle $T_0=6$ hours and bottleneck rate $r_b=0.4$ jobs per hour, and the target throughput is $0.3$ jobs per hour. What does the bound $\mathrm{TH}_1(n)\leq\min\{n/T_0,\,r_b\}$ alone show about the card count $n$?
options: At least 2 cards are necessary, but it does not show that 2 suffice.
2 cards suffice, since $2/T_0\approx0.33$ is above the target of $0.3$.
1 card suffices, since the target $0.3$ is below the bottleneck rate $0.4$.
2 cards are necessary and give a throughput of exactly $2/T_0=1/3$.
